findings.criterion: Unresolved bug candidate 5bd7-33ec-8630-440e — Agentic verdicts skip drift floor and cross-checks (Epic Goal 2 / AC 1: same verdict contract; ADR records the agentic design)
findings.detail: The bug describes a defect in what this epic built. Under the agentic engine, `_run_plan_review` skips the pipeline-only post-dispatch tail: the drift floor, the cross-checks (`xcheck`) that rewrite `blocking`, the rising and completion floors, and fix-unit grouping. So the two engines can sign different verdict strings and blocking lists for the same plan material and findings. ADR 0123 documents only the Layer-1 floor and claimability running first under both engines. It does not say the tail is pipeline-only or justify that. The bug is open and in planning. It has no `supersedes`/`duplicates` link and no reasoned deferral or pre-existence statement. Its only link is `discovered_from` this epic. The epic's own comments call the tail gap an advisory 'not filed here' as a follow-up, which is not a disposition on the bug itself.
findings.remediation: Either run the drift floor and cross-checks on agentic verdicts, or amend ADR 0123 to state and justify that they are pipeline-only, with a test pinning the choice under both engines. Alternatively, record a reasoned disposition on the bug (a named successor ticket, or a concrete deferral rationale).

citations.description: Ticket e57f-200d-d402-4a5e description and ACs: 0-tool-call run must resolve INDETERMINATE and mint no attestation; no disposition visible in the snapshot I read.

findings.criterion: Unresolved bug candidate e57f-200d-d402-4a5e — Agentic plan review signs a PASS with zero tool calls (Epic fail-closed invariant and AC on INDETERMINATE for incomplete runs)
findings.detail: The bug describes a defect in the epic's agentic engine. `adapt_findings` builds the verdict from the findings list alone. Nothing checks how many tool calls the agent made, so a run that answers `{"findings": []}` without reading any code gets a non-blocking PASS and a certified attestation that the claim gate accepts. The pipeline engine has no such hole, and the epic's 'fail closed' invariant is meant to stop silent approvals. The bug is open and in planning. It has no `supersedes`/`duplicates` link and no reasoned deferral. Its only link is `discovered_from` this epic. The epic's comment listing it as an advisory 'not filed here' is not a recorded disposition on the bug.
findings.remediation: Fix it: make a 0-tool-call agentic run INDETERMINATE through the `resolution_class` path, and record the tool-call count on coverage. Or record a reasoned deferral or successor ticket on the bug that states why the behaviour is acceptable.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, the criterion needs the exact `[non-codebase]` tag at the start of the checkbox text, `- [ ] [non-codebase] <criterion>`, and an indented continuation line directly under it, `provenance: environment=<v>; principal=<v>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <justification>`. If the reviewed plan did not already carry both, add them in one description edit: that edit changes the reviewed plan and stales the plan-review attestation, so run `rebar review-plan` on this ticket before closing again. Then add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet the criterion (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion); comments are non-material, so a criterion tagged before review needs only the comment. The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
